MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 8, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on July 8, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on July 3, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Ruesch presented certificates of commendation to the "Marine of the Quarter"
  Corporal Jose GonzalezMorales, "Non-Commissioned Officer of the Quarter" Corporal Jalen
  Coston, and Junior Sailor of the Quarter HM2 (FMF) Justin Harris.

City Council Minutes  1  July 8, 2025
 P2. Proclaim Mid-Summer through Early Autumn 2025 To Be Wildfire Awareness &
  Prevention Season

  Mayor Ruesch presented proclamation to Fire Chief Cheyne Maule.

P3. Recognize the Rotary Club on Their 50th Anniversary

  Mayor Ruesch presented proclamation Paul Bucknum and former Rotary President Millard
  Roth.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michael Rochter, M.V.: Thanked the sheriff’s department for their prompt action in pulling over a
driver at last week’s rally that intentionally emitted exhaust around the protestors. Questioned why
this person received only a warning that was not given to his colleague that received a ticket for
temporary stopping in a bus zone to unload items for the rally.

Sam Lewis, M.V.: Expressed his gratefulness to those that challenge his beliefs because it helps
him to grow.

Aleksander Climidzic, M.V.: Spoke on the Community of Character Word of the Month “Fairness”

Gene Dery, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the Cordova Community and voiced his concerns about the
illegal fireworks at Cordova Park in his neighborhood this past fourth of July.

Kira Blick, M.V.: Spoke on the artificial light that affects the migration of birds and encouraged
the Council to consider the Audubon Lights Out Program.

Carolyn Gatto, M.V.: Thanked the OCSD for the police presence at the last rally. Questioned if the
sidewalks are being scheduled for repairs and asked to be notified when that will be taking place.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Thanked everyone who made this year’s Saddleback College Pride Event a
success — growing from 1,800 to over 2,000 attendees and nearly doubling the booths. He gave a
special thanks to Councilmember Cynthia Vasquez and Dr. Elliot Stein, who attended. Voiced
concerns that the DEI Task Force, which supported last year’s event, seems to have been dissolved
without public notice. Thanked Councilmember Brian Goodell for helping start that group.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Stated in 2007, the City hired the Urban Land Institute to assess the Village
Center area. Their report raised key issues like fragmented ownership, but their involvement
ended—partly due to a mixed-use proposal. I’m requesting a full financial report on Phase One
before moving to Phase Two, we need a clear picture of where we’ve been and what it cost.

Robert Breton, M.V.: Stated that prayer has historically played an important role in American
government, dating back to the Constitutional Convention and that the Founders designed the First
Amendment to prevent religious domination while still allowing public officials to seek divine
guidance. He pointed out that the First Amendment protects freedom of religion, allowing public
officials to seek divine guidance without promoting a specific faith

City Council Minutes  6  July 8, 2025
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell had the honor of attending the Pacific Mini Games in Palau this past
week, invited by ONOC (Oceania National Olympic Committees) through the Nadadores
Foundation. The goal: identify swimming talent from across Oceania for a development program
leading up to the 2028 Olympics in LA, with training camps based in Mission Viejo. He observed
four days of swimming events, evaluating athletes from countries like Fiji, Tahiti, Palau, Guam,
and New Caledonia. He stated that some showed real promise, and he will be submitting
recommendations for future camp invitations. He stated it was a long trip — 22 hours each way and
a 16-hour time difference — but a great opportunity to support Olympic development in the region
and build stronger relationships with ONOC and partner nations. He is excited to be part of this
journey to 2028!

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked Congresswoman Young Kim for her dedication in renaming the
Mission Viejo Post Office as the Majo Megan McClung Post Office. Megan, a Mission Viejo native
and outstanding Marine who died in the line of duty, deserves this honor. It took years and great
perseverance from Congresswoman Kim to make this happen, showing her deep care for our
community and service members. The dedication ceremony was meaningful, with Megan’s family,
classmates, and community members in attendance. She also enjoyed the Mission Viejo Street
Fair—big thanks to the Activities Committee and city staff for making it such a great event. She
stated that the city’s summer camps at Montanoso and Sierra Recreation Centers may be still open;
check the Mission Viejo Life for details. Lastly, the City Council will be on break until the end of
August.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated she is very familiar with those summer camps. Her youngest has
done the flag football camp and is currently in a volleyball camp at the YMCA in Laguna Niguel,
since her original camp was canceled that week. Next week, she’ll be in the tennis camp, and she’s
also done basketball and will be doing golf soon. Council Member Vasquez missed the post office
renaming ceremony because her daughter had a scrimmage on the last day of flag football. She said
that picking her up from volleyball camp today reminded her of when her older daughter started
playing sports at eight. She attended the Fourth of July Street Fair, walked around, and spent the
day with friends. Lastly, she introduced her husband and daughter sitting in the audience.

City Council Minutes  7  July 8, 2025
 Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum supported Council Member Kelly’s comments on the post office
renaming, noting that although Congresswoman Kim had to return to D.C. for a vote, Supervisor
Don Wagner delivered a strong, unscripted speech in her place. She attended the Fourth of July
Street Fair and thanked a resident for voicing concerns about fireworks in neighborhoods. She also
attended the symphony at Napoli Park and praised the large turnout. Bucknum reminded residents
about several upcoming events: Shakespeare in the Park at Oso Viejo Community Park this week
at 7 p.m., the Fire Station 24 grand opening next Thursday afternoon, National Night Out on July
31 at the Youth Athletic Park, and Prelude in the Park on Saturday, August 9.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch recently attended the SCOR Appreciation Lunch to recognize and thank the
dedicated volunteers who support our city and police services in countless ways. Their commitment
and service are deeply valued by the entire community. On June 28, the Mayor also participated in
the annual Amateur Radio Field Day at Gilleran Park. This important event showcases the
capabilities of amateur radio operators—individuals who play a critical role in emergency
preparedness. In times of catastrophe, when power and communication systems might fail, these
volunteers are the ones who can step in to help maintain essential communication. They generously
invest their time and personal resources to ensure we are never without a lifeline when it matters
most. Mayor Ruesch also shared exciting news: the city will host its first Annual Barbecue Battle,
a music and barbecue festival featuring top Pit Masters competing in a contest. The event will take
place at the Village Green from July 25–27 and will include an amateur barbecue competition—
which the Mayor himself will help judge! He closed his remarks with a motivational quote:
“Motivation is what gets you started. Habit is what keeps you going.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:18 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday August 26, 2025.
